tracks.title: PyTorch foundations
tracks.summary: Build a complete training workflow from tensors, autograd, modules, data pipelines, and convolutional networks.

tracks.title: Modern generative models
tracks.summary: Reach transformers and diffusion after a compact foundation in tensors, learning, modules, and convolution.

tracks.title: Medical imaging project
tracks.summary: Prepare for the CT project, then follow data engineering, classification, evaluation, and segmentation end to end.

tracks.title: Scaling and production
tracks.summary: Start from a reliable training baseline, then study distributed execution, profiling, export, and deployment.

tracks.title: Experienced-user fast track
tracks.summary: Review current PyTorch contracts and move directly to the modern-model and systems chapters.

checkpoints.title: Environment checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Run the device check and explain every printed field before continuing.

checkpoints.title: Workflow checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Annotate data, model, loss, backward, and optimizer in one complete training step.

checkpoints.title: Inference checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Verify preprocessing, evaluation mode, inference mode, device, and output shape.

checkpoints.title: Training bridge
checkpoints.action: Identify what changes when moving from pretrained inference to a trainable classifier.

checkpoints.title: Shape checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Predict the result shape of three broadcasts before running them.

checkpoints.title: Modern API checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Replace the historical named-tensor idea with positional layout checks.

checkpoints.title: Representation checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Write the axes, dtype, range, units, and normalization source for one sample.

checkpoints.title: Modality checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Compare the tensor contract of two different data modalities.

checkpoints.title: Gradient checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Trace which tensors are leaves, which track history, and where gradients accumulate.

checkpoints.title: Loop checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Run a guarded training loop and diagnose one deliberately broken configuration.

checkpoints.title: Module checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Explain registration, forward(), and the input/output contract of a custom module.

checkpoints.title: Parity checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Compare eager and compiled outputs before discussing performance.

checkpoints.title: Data boundary checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Inspect one train batch and one validation batch for shape, dtype, label mapping, and transform policy.

checkpoints.title: Evaluation checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Select on validation data and touch the reserved test split only after selection.

checkpoints.title: CNN shape checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Calculate every spatial shape by hand and confirm it with a synthetic batch.

checkpoints.title: Performance checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Separate correctness parity, cold start, and warm latency in one comparison.

checkpoints.title: Attention checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Draw the causal matrix and verify handwritten attention against SDPA.

checkpoints.title: Token checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Compare sequence tokens and image patches using one shared shape vocabulary.

checkpoints.title: Denoiser checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Verify timestep, image, and prediction shapes for both U-Net and transformer denoisers.

checkpoints.title: Sampling checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Separate sample quality, eager parity, cold compilation, and warm execution.

checkpoints.title: Leakage checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Prove that patient or series identities cannot cross dataset partitions.

checkpoints.title: Project checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Write the evidence required before each claimed project milestone.

checkpoints.title: Geometry checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Round-trip a known physical point and state the error in millimeters.

checkpoints.title: Dataset checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Inspect representative crops with source identity and preprocessing metadata visible.

checkpoints.title: Classifier checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Overfit a tiny batch before starting a full training run.

checkpoints.title: Resume checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Restore all required state and reproduce the next controlled update.

checkpoints.title: Imbalance checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Compare weighting and sampling without changing the evaluation distribution.

checkpoints.title: Selection checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Record one validation-selected decision before final test evaluation.

checkpoints.title: Provenance checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Trace one generated mask back to its source scan, prompt, model, and review status.

checkpoints.title: Transfer checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Compare transfer quality, prompt sensitivity, latency, licensing, and failure modes.

checkpoints.title: DDP checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Launch a small job, verify data coverage, synchronized parameters, and clean shutdown.

checkpoints.title: Scaling checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Choose DDP, FSDP2, tensor parallelism, or pipeline parallelism from a measured constraint.

checkpoints.title: Artifact checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Test eager, compiled, and exported parity at every declared shape boundary.

checkpoints.title: Deployment checkpoint
checkpoints.action: Write a decision record covering runtime, device, quality, latency, memory, and provenance.

glossary.definition: The recorded tensor operations that PyTorch traverses backward to calculate gradients.
A group of examples processed together in one model call.
Rules that align tensor dimensions from the right and virtually reuse size-one dimensions.
Saved model and training state used for inference, evaluation, or a controlled restart.
A distributed operation in which a defined group of ranks communicates in the same order.
Information from validation or test data influencing training, preprocessing statistics, or model selection.
The processor and memory location that own a tensor or execute an operation.
The numeric representation used by every element of a tensor.
Normal PyTorch execution in which Python operations run immediately and remain directly inspectable.
One traversal of the selected training samples, usually divided into batches.
Module state used for evaluation; it changes behavior of modules such as Dropout and BatchNorm but does not disable gradients.
A derivative describing how a scalar objective changes with respect to a tensor or parameter.
A context that disables autograd recording and related tracking when outputs will not be used for training.
A tensor created directly rather than as the result of a tracked operation; learnable parameters are leaves.
An unnormalized model score supplied directly to losses such as cross entropy or BCE with logits.
A scalar training signal measuring the current prediction error under a chosen objective.
A PyTorch object that registers parameters, buffers, and child modules and defines a forward computation.
An algorithm that updates registered parameters using their accumulated gradients.
Extra values introduced to control spatial shape or make variable-length sequences rectangular.
A registered tensor whose value is normally learned through gradient-based optimization.
One process in a distributed job; world size is the number of participating processes.
The documented size and semantic meaning of every tensor axis at a boundary.
A mapping from registered module or optimizer state names to tensors and primitive values.
A multidimensional array with one shape, dtype, device, and application-specific meaning.
Data used to select models, thresholds, and other choices without updating parameters.
